## My Reasoning

We have about 8 mu of land, flat and good for the wheat-maize rotation everyone here does. My husband goes to Handan for construction work half the year, so I manage the fields myself. I have no reason to try anything different — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same as my parents, same as all my neighbors. The land is familiar to me.

For wheat, I'll buy Zhengmai seeds from the seed shop in town — the shopkeeper says they yield well and resist disease. I rotary-till after the maize harvest in October, then sow. I put down diammonium phosphate and a bag of urea as base fertilizer, then I topdress before the spring watering. Three irrigations: one before the ground freezes, one at jointing, one when the heads are filling. I spray herbicide in January and then spray again for rust and aphids before heading. That's 3 pesticide times.

For maize, I sow it right into the wheat stubble with the small seeder I borrow from my brother-in-law — no need to till. I always use hybrid seed, everyone does, the yield is much better. I put compound fertilizer down at seeding and then topdress a big bag of urea at jointing stage. Summer rain is usually enough but I'll irrigate once if August is dry. Just two sprays — herbicide right after seeding, and one for corn borer if I see moths.
